traits.leaf_length_m.note: Flora of North America (vol. 2), Athyrium filix-femina var. cyclosorum, the northwestern lady fern of the Puget Sound lowlands: "Petiole 15--45(--60) cm, base densely scaly; scales brown or dark brown, lanceolate or ovate-lanceolate, (7--)10--20 × (1--)2--5 mm, ± crisped. Blade elliptic to oblanceolate, 1--2-pinnate-pinnatifid, 25--120 × 10--50 cm"; the species: "Petiole straw-colored distally ... base dark red-brown or black, swollen". Read as 25 to 120 cm.

traits.petiole_length_m.note: Flora of North America (vol. 2), Athyrium filix-femina var. cyclosorum, the northwestern lady fern of the Puget Sound lowlands: "Petiole 15--45(--60) cm, base densely scaly; scales brown or dark brown, lanceolate or ovate-lanceolate, (7--)10--20 × (1--)2--5 mm, ± crisped. traits.note: Abrams's flora (vol. 1, 1923; ferns by Maxon): rhizome erect or ascending; fronds up to 2 m, erect and arching, on short stipes; blades lanceolate, narrowed at both ends, two or three times pinnate, their segments toothed to cut again (so typically three); sori under 1 mm, oblong to crescent- or horseshoe-shaped.

generator.params.note: Hand-set from general knowledge of the species: a delicate, deciduous fern: a vase of soft, lacy, twice-divided fronds widest in the middle. Not fitted to measurements. Frond length and stipe share (visual forms fern stipes, 2026-10-17) now come from the blade and petiole Flora of North America gives (traits), in place of a hand-set 1.15 m frond with a stipe 0.12 of it, which the flora's "blades ca. 2 times length of petioles" contradicts.

allometry.note: Rough sizes from general knowledge of the species: 1 m tall at 4 years in the open. Replace with measured data before calling this species calibrated.

appearance.note: Colours chosen by eye: light yellow-green fronds. Its stipes take their stated colour (stipe_colour).

taxon.note: Scientific and common names (and USDA symbol, where given) as the spec's authors wrote them, and the genus the scientific name is written in.

growth_form.note: The growth form the spec's authors chose from the plant's habit.

growth.note: The growth plan (years, step, keyframes) chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

variants.note: The environments, conditions and seeds chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

taxon.family.note: WCVP v16's family for the accepted name.

traits.rhizome_habit.note: The spec's value is from its `traits` note (abrams-1923). Hoshizaki and Moran, Fern Grower's Manual (2001) p. 207-210: rhizome short-creeping to erect, clump-forming. The spec stated {"erect": "usually", "ascending": "often"}. Combined on the owner's rule (2026-10-15): where two sources differ, both are kept and the range spans them.
